excipients.name: Phospholipid complex (phytosome)
excipients.mechanism: Forms a lipid-compatible complex with polyphenols, raising dissolution and membrane partitioning.

excipients.name: Hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin
excipients.mechanism: Forms an inclusion complex that solubilises lipophilic actives and shields labile groups.

excipients.name: Self-emulsifying lipid (SEDDS)
excipients.mechanism: Presents the active pre-dissolved in fine oil droplets; promotes lymphatic uptake, bypassing first-pass.

excipients.name: Amorphous solid dispersion (PVP)
excipients.mechanism: Traps the active in an amorphous, rapidly dissolving polymer matrix.

excipients.name: Vitamin E TPGS
excipients.mechanism: Non-ionic surfactant that solubilises and inhibits P-glycoprotein efflux.

excipients.name: Piperine (BioPerine®)
excipients.mechanism: Inhibits intestinal UGT glucuronidation and P-gp efflux, cutting first-pass loss.

excipients.name: Labrasol (caprylocaproyl macrogolglycerides)
excipients.mechanism: Surfactant that fluidises enterocyte membranes and solubilises the active.

excipients.name: Chitosan
excipients.mechanism: Opens epithelial tight junctions and prolongs mucosal contact time.

excipients.name: Quercetin (co-active)
excipients.mechanism: Competes for UGT/SULT conjugation, sparing the primary active from first-pass metabolism.

excipients.name: α-Tocopherol (antioxidant)
excipients.mechanism: Scavenges radicals that drive oxidative degradation of the active.

excipients.name: pH / citrate buffer
excipients.mechanism: Holds a pH where the active resists hydrolytic / alkaline degradation (e.g. curcumin at neutral pH).

excipients.name: Liposomal encapsulation
excipients.mechanism: Encloses the active in a phospholipid bilayer — physical protection plus improved uptake.
